meta.themes: Debt-Financed Compute, Production Agent Stacks, Frontier Models Turned Defensive, Consumer AI Distribution

news.title: Nvidia guaranteed up to $105B of OpenAI's Ohio data center lease
news.summary: Nvidia agreed to backstop up to $105 billion of OpenAI's 20-year lease on a Pike County, Ohio campus being developed by SoftBank-owned SB Energy, and separately invested $1.5 billion in SB Energy, in exchange for being the exclusive chip supplier to a site slated to reach as much as 8 gigawatts.

news.title: Broadcom sought more than $60B in debt to finance AI chips for Anthropic
news.summary: Broadcom entered talks with lenders including Blackstone and Apollo on a special-purpose-vehicle financing that could total as much as $100 billion—roughly $60-70 billion of partly guaranteed senior secured notes plus about $30 billion of junior debt—to fund custom chip capacity for Anthropic and other AI companies.

news.title: Anthropic took its production agent stack out of beta
news.summary: Computer use, a new browser use tool, the Skills API, and the Files API all reached general availability on the Claude Platform, with the updated computer toolset batching several actions per turn instead of one per model call, HIPAA eligibility under Anthropic's BAA, and 1 TB of file storage per organization at 5x the previous rate limits.

news.title: Anthropic pointed its most cyber-capable model at defenders
news.summary: Claude Security scans now run on Claude Mythos 5—the model Anthropic says has the strongest cybersecurity capabilities in the world and had restricted to vetted partners—delivered as scan results rather than a prompt box so it cannot be steered into writing exploits, alongside a $35 million credit fund for securing open-source software.

news.title: VS Code 1.134 introduced an agent host shared across windows
news.summary: The release added an agent host that runs agent harnesses in a dedicated process on the new Agent Host Protocol, letting multiple VS Code windows attach to the same agent session, with its Copilot harness powered by the Copilot SDK so behavior matches Copilot CLI and the standalone Copilot app.

news.title: Claude's Workspace connectors gained write access as Cowork went broad
news.summary: Anthropic's Google Workspace connectors moved beyond reading to sending email in Gmail and managing files in Google Drive, and access to Claude Cowork on mobile and web rolled out to all paid accounts so users can supervise agent work from more places.

news.title: Stripe confirmed it is buying OpenRouter for a reported $7.5B
news.summary: Stripe outbid interested parties including Databricks for the AI model gateway, paying roughly $7.5 billion according to New York Times sources—about six times OpenRouter's $1.3 billion valuation in May—in a move that pushes the payments company into managing AI spend rather than only collecting it.

news.title: Meta quietly became one of Microsoft's largest AI customers
news.summary: Meta is spending hundreds of millions of dollars a year and running trillions of tokens a week through Azure to reach outside models via Microsoft Foundry—partly to benchmark its own systems—even as it builds a competing API business, a pairing that renews questions about how circular AI demand has become.

news.title: Google gave college students a free year of its paid AI plans
news.summary: Eligible US college students get 12 months of Google AI Pro and students elsewhere get Google AI Plus at no cost, bundled with a new Gemini student hub, study notebooks with calendar integration, generated 3D simulations in Search and Gemini, and Deep Research reports you can request and discuss by voice in Gemini Live.

news.title: FDA floated competency exams for generative AI medical devices
news.summary: A CDRH discussion paper proposed evaluating generative AI-enabled devices the way clinicians are credentialed—benchmarking the final user-facing product against a panel or median clinician using scoring rubrics and expert adjudication, then leaning harder on postmarket monitoring—with comments open until October 19 under docket FDA-2026-N-7874.

news.title: OpenAI funded 14 outside projects to stress-test its own policy agenda
news.summary: Following through on a commitment in its April industrial policy paper, OpenAI awarded $1 million in grants plus up to $1 million in API credits across 14 organizations spanning the US, EU, Brazil, Singapore, and South Korea—including the American Enterprise Institute, the Progressive Policy Institute, and the Nuclear Threat Initiative—selected from more than 400 responses.

news.title: Meta opened its vibe-coding app Pocket to all US users
news.summary: Pocket, built on Meta Superintelligence Labs' Muse Spark model and grown out of the Gizmo acqui-hire, lets anyone prompt small interactive games that publish to a scrollable feed where others can play, save, or remix them—Meta's bet that AI creation becomes a social format rather than another app-store download.
